summary:
This is a rapid-fire startup showcase, not a single-architecture talk. Diego Rodriguez, co-founder and CTO at Korea (ASR for a creative-suite company), opens with three stories: cars were easy to invent once you had wheels and an engine, but traffic was the surprise; Tower of Babel as standup-meeting language wars; a Netflix contact asking how to find town-level personalized content in India. His job is to ask what “traffics” AI is missing—JSON, MCP, and a million images a day for one studio. He says Korea already went from signup to paid Fox broadcast ads in two days, flashes 25 million raised and an eight-person team, then yields the stage.

OpenHome pitches the first AI-driven smart speaker: 500 million speakers sold last year still use awkward command language. The founder cites Splunk, a $5B MakerDo developer ecosystem, and a sold $50M privacy company, then claims 10,000 developers building toys, robots, appliances, and home-automation apps on a jailbroken, open, LLM-driven kit. They release 500 free dev kits to the room.

Josh (Koframe) says a prior company hit $2B and he shipped a briefly #1 GitHub autonomous coding agent. The internet is “dead”—sites are not adaptive—so Koframe gives every customer experience its own AI growth team. Claims: $20M for Europe’s largest travel company in weeks, CTR lift for a $400B Indian enterprise, exclusive OpenAI marketing-tech partnership.

Eugene (Federous AI) says his team built Quorki 72B without transformer attention on eight GPUs, 1000× cheaper inference, techniques reusable as speculative decoding. Hot take: scale is dead; DeepMind and “Lun” want new architectures; >90% of production AI projects fail on reliability. Companies need agents that book tickets and file taxes at 99.9%, not PhD math. Action R1 is said to beat Claude, Gemini, and OpenAI on reliable form-filling. Tagline: reliability is revenue.

Jonas (Upside), ex-Branch (deep links; 100M-user search), does forensic revenue attribution. GTM teams hoard Salesforce data but cannot use it. LLMs extract structure the way crawlers structured the web, producing a knowledge-graph command center. A LinkedIn post produced a “who’s who” waitlist. Hiring: graphs, analytics agents, graph learning.

Sua (Open Audio, formerly Fish Audio) jokes “Open AI,” then cites 400K→$5.5M ARR in four months and a $100M C-round. Origin story: build an AI you can fall in love with, starting with voice. S1 is “the first instructible voice model” (what and how). Live at fish.audio; claims they beat ElevenLabs on TTS Arena.

David Vorick (Glow; Siacoin $10k→$3B) raised $30M from Framework and USV, claims a $10M single-day on-chain DePIN revenue record. Glow pays for solar with tokens, not shovels; an India farm was built to mine Glow. Projects in India, Mexico, Lebanon. Email davidglowabs.org.

A second David: 250M-user social app at $20M/year, now building Favored, “world’s most engaging app,” 1→$100M ARR claim, hiring.

Alex Atala (Open Router; OpenC 2017) asked whether inference is winner-take-all. A BYO-model Chrome extension became a single API over all LLMs: pay once, near-zero switch cost, tool calling, caching, regional prices, chat comparison, privacy controls, observability, and public rankings. Thesis: inference is a commodity—Claude on Bedrock, Vertex, and Anthropic should match. Middleware “plugins” can call MCPs and transform outputs. Roadmap: images, enterprise, prompt observability. Careers page.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.
temporalContext: Transcript claims reflect the publication date; linked external context was checked at the run's research date.
takeaways: The session is a multi-founder lightning reel: creative-suite discovery, voice hardware, growth agents, reliability AGI, GTM graphs, instructible TTS, solar DePIN, social, and an LLM marketplace.
Diego’s frame: the hard AI problem is the “traffic” after generation—finding the right artifact among a million images or personalized ads.
OpenHome bets on natural voice plus a jailbroken developer ecosystem, not command-based smart speakers.
Koframe’s product claim is a per-site AI growth team with named enterprise lifts and an OpenAI partnership.
Federous argues production AI fails on reliability, not IQ; Action R1 is positioned as form-filling reliability over frontier math.
Upside uses LLMs to structure abused CRM data into a knowledge-graph command center for sales and marketing.
Open Audio S1 is pitched as instructible TTS (content and delivery) and is live at fish.audio.
Open Router’s thesis is commodity inference: one API, homogeneous Claude across clouds, plus plugins that wrap MCP.

organization.name: Krea
organization.summary: Krea (krea.ai) is an independent San Francisco generative-media company founded by Diego Rodriguez Prado and Víctor Pérez. First-party pages describe an AI creative suite for images, video, 3D, realtime generation, enhancement, LoRA training, and a node editor, plus Krea 2, a foundation image model trained from scratch. Docs expose a REST API over the same models. The conference speaker page and Diego’s own site confirm he is co-founder and CTO. This video is a multi-startup HF0 residency reel; Krea is the opening speaker’s employer and the first implementation discussed. Other pitches (OpenHome, Featherless AI / ASR Federous, Upside, Open Audio, Glow, Open Router) are separate companies, not parents or vendors of Krea.
organization.status: Independent company as of the research date. Homepage, docs, user guide, enterprise product, and API introduction are live. No ownership change since the August 2025 talk.
